correctness.rationale: The defining Wigner integral gives the checked exact quartic Gaussian factor. The radial quadratic discriminant has positive roots only under cos(2theta)<sqrt(2)t-sqrt(1+t²); monotonicity identifies the sole transition t=2sqrt(2). Differentiating both polar variables and checking the origin isolates the only singularities; the t-critical factorization and Hessian diag(96,-32) are exact. Gaussian upper tail outside the minimum negative radius and a small disk of negative values at p=2^(-1/4)t^(-1/2) squeeze the negative-mass logarithmic exponent to -1/sqrt(2). Exact symbolic moment, factorization, sign and numerical defining-integral checks were executed from the packaged checker; sampled calculations are corroborative, not proofs. Boundary convention uses strict interiors/exteriors.

value.rationale: The lowest nontrivial even Hermite superposition is a canonical continuous-variable Fourier/Wigner test case. Its negativity changes from two disconnected islands to a connected annulus at one exact amplitude, with a remarkable factorization into intersecting geometric circles and rigorously quantified exponentially remote near-vacuum negativity. A complete parameter-dependent nodal classification and sharp nonperturbative exponent answer motivated geometric/spectral questions not implied by the polynomial identity or general qualitative Hudson negativity theorem; the result is not merely an arbitrary sampled polynomial or a finite recomputation.
